what_its_for: Molindone is used to treat schizophrenia. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), delusions (false beliefs), and disorganized thinking. It belongs to a group of medicines called antipsychotics.
how_to_take: Take molindone by mouth, exactly as your doctor prescribed. You can take it with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how you respond to the medicine. The usual starting dose for adults is 50 to 75 mg per day, divided into smaller doses taken throughout the day. Your doctor may adjust your dose up to 225 mg per day if needed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store molindone at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking molindone — it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may make side effects worse. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Avoid suddenly stopping this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause your symptoms to return.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: stiff muscles, high fever, confusion, or fast heartbeat (these could be signs of a rare but serious condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); uncontrolled movements of your face, tongue, or body (this could be a condition called tardive dyskinesia); severe dizziness or fainting; signs of infection like fever or sore throat; difficulty swallowing or breathing; thoughts of harming yourself. Also call your doctor if you feel more depressed, notice worsening symptoms, or have any new or concerning side effects.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within the first few days to weeks of treatment. However, it may take several weeks (sometimes 4 to 6 weeks or longer) to feel the full benefit of this medicine. It is important to keep taking it even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, falls, and movement problems. This medicine may also increase the risk of serious events in older adults with dementia-related psychosis — talk to your doctor about the risks. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers who took antipsychotics in the third trimester may have temporary withdrawal symptoms or movement problems after birth. Breastfeeding: It is not known if molindone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been well established. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits.
